plants.name: Colchicum autumnale
plants.description: Pale lilac-pink goblets rise straight from bare soil, with no leaves in sight. They carpet damp meadows and woodland edges just as the autumn colors turn.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late summer to mid-autumn (typically September to October)
plants.location: Meadows and woodlands of Western and Central Europe, including the UK, France and Germany
plants.funFact: Autumn crocus is not a true crocus. It belongs to the lily relatives, and its leaves appear in spring and die back long before the flowers emerge. Every part of the plant is highly toxic, and it is the natural source of colchicine, a compound used in medicine and plant breeding.

plants.name: Jacaranda mimosifolia
plants.description: Whole streets and hillsides turn hazy violet-blue as trumpet-shaped flowers open in huge clusters over fern-like foliage. Fallen blossoms carpet the pavement beneath the trees.
plants.bloomingSeason: Spring in the Southern Hemisphere (roughly October to November)
plants.location: Pretoria and Johannesburg in South Africa, plus Sydney, Brisbane and Buenos Aires
plants.funFact: Jacaranda is native to South America but is now planted in warm cities around the world. In Pretoria, thousands of street trees earned the city the nickname Jacaranda City. Local lore in some places says a falling bloom brings good luck.

plants.name: Chrysanthemum × morifolium
plants.description: Dense mounds of daisy-like or pom-pom blooms light up autumn gardens and balconies, long after most other flowers have faded. Cool nights make the colors deepen.
plants.bloomingSeason: Autumn (typically September to November) in the Northern Hemisphere
plants.location: Gardens across East Asia, Europe and North America, with a long tradition in Japan and China
plants.funFact: Chrysanthemums flower in response to shortening days. Growers can bring them into bloom out of season by covering the plants to mimic long nights. The flower is also a symbol of the Japanese imperial family.
